lacuna.repo_anchor: plan/0005-format-interop/README.md Stages 6-7 - stage 6: 'FP8 activations (W8A8 emulated): per-token scales; activations rounded onto the E4M3 grid but stored and computed in FP16 (faithful emulation, no hardware FP8 needed); runtime quantization hook at the layer boundary'; stage 7: 'FP8 KV: recast to fp16 KV at 2x memory (faithful, simple) or int8 KV (measured against fp16-KV quality); the serving config records which the checkpoint requires'; grounded by the plan/0005 hardware-fact sheet ('E4M3 in FP16: lossless (subset); rebias = +8 to the exponent field') and stage 11 ('the largest blocked surface is not a format: upstream V1 requires FlashAttention or FlashInfer (sm 80+)... This fork retains the Turing-capable engine'); MEMORY.md 2026-08-27 - 'INT8 is exactly twice FP16 at 203 TOPS' and 'every ALU kind contends with the HMMA stream' (the native-track ceiling the item must account).
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-07 the surface splits into five live threads. (1) FP8 KV upstream state: vLLM's FP8 KV surface (kv_cache_dtype fp8/fp8_e4m3/fp8_e5m2, per-tensor or per-attention-head scales, calibration via llm-compressor, --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers from #33695) is documented and was validated in the vLLM blog 'The State of FP8 KV-Cache and Attention Quantization' (2026-04-22) on H100/FA3, H200/FlashMLA, and B200/FlashInfer only - it found and fixed an FA3 imprecise-FP32-accumulation bug that dropped 128k needle-in-a-haystack accuracy from 91 percent (BF16) to 13 percent (FP8), restored to 89 percent by a two-level-accumulation fix; conclusion: FP8 KV is near-baseline and the recommended default for decode-heavy long-context serving (best-case decode ITL slope 54 percent of BF16, +14.9 percent throughput), but avoid below ~7k-token contexts, head_dim 256 prefill, and uncalibrated scales below 95 percent recovery. No pre-sm80 hardware appears anywhere in it. (2) The Turing regression hole: vLLM issue #47549 (ptempier, filed 2026-07-03, OPEN, no maintainer response, no linked fix) documents that v0.23.0 auto-selected FlashInfer on SM75 from candidates ['FLASHINFER', 'TRITON_ATTN'] and FP8 KV worked there via software conversion (flashinfer-python 0.6.12) - 287,744-token KV cache on a Quadro RTX 8000 (TP2+PP2, ~22k context) decoding at ~5-11 tok/s - while v0.24.0 (~2026-06-29, 571 commits, per-KV-cache-group backend selection #48012) offers only TRITON_ATTN on SM75 and rejects --kv-cache-dtype fp8 with 'FP8 KV cache is not supported by the Triton attention backend... native FP8 (fp8e4nv) requires SM89+'; forced fp16 KV halves capacity to ~143k tokens and decode collapses ~10x to 0.8-1.1 tok/s from scheduler preemption; the reporter attributes the removal to the backend-selection refactor in vllm/v1/attention/backends/cuda.py and suspects PR #46492 (FLASHINFER_CUTLASS NVFP4 MoE clamp) [uncertain: causation is the reporter's analysis, unconfirmed]; 18 GPUs affected on the reporting cluster (T4 through RTX 8000). The current docs matrix codifies the gate: FLASHINFER Native = compute cap 8.x-9.x, FLASH_ATTN FA2 >= 8.0, FA3 9.x, FA4 >= 10.0, TRITON_ATTN = Any. FlashInfer itself still lists SM75-and-later support and ships sm75 wheels, but FlashInfer issue #3620 (2026-06-12, priority P1, assigned, fix PR #3621 still open) shows BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCache failing on first launch on SM75: the prefill launcher's shared-memory estimate omits k/v scale buffers and alignment padding, so sizeof(SharedStorage) lands just over the 64 KB sm75 opt-in limit (SM80+'s 164 KB masks the miscount) - i.e. even re-selecting FlashInfer on sm75 does not currently yield a working prefill. (3) TurboQuant: the paper family is TurboQuant (arXiv:2504.19874, Zandieh/Daliri/Hadian/Mirrokni, submitted 2025-04-28; ICLR 2026), PolarQuant (arXiv:2502.02617, AISTATS 2026), and QJL (arXiv:2406.03482, AAAI); Google Research blog post 2026-03-24 (Zandieh and Mirrokni, with collaborators incl. Majid Hadian of Google DeepMind, Insu Han KAIST, Majid Daliri NYU) claims 3-bit KV 'without requiring training or fine-tuning and causing any compromise in model accuracy', zero quantization-constant overhead (the 1-2 bits/number tax of conventional quantizers), at least 6x KV memory reduction with perfect needle-in-a-haystack, and up to 8x speedup for 4-bit keys on H100; the method is data-oblivious (random rotations induce a concentrated Beta distribution, then optimal per-coordinate scalar quantization; online, no calibration). Upstream vLLM integration landed as PR #38479 (vibhavagarwal5, opened 2026-03-29, merged 2026-04-15, mgoin-approved): a dedicated TurboQuantAttentionBackend with store/decode as fused Triton kernels plus CUDA sources (tq_store_cuda.cu) and prefill via flash_attn_varlen_func, exposing four presets - turboquant_k8v4 (2.6x compression, GSM8K 0.860 vs 0.900 base), turboquant_4bit_nc (3.8x, 0.840), turboquant_k3v4_nc (4.3x, 0.780), turboquant_3bit_nc (4.9x, 0.720); FP8 K casts auto-select tl.float8e4nv (Hopper+) vs tl.float8e4b15 (Ampere); benchmarked on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, with community runs on H100, 8x RTX A4000 (SM86), and DGX Spark GB10 (Triton fallback); hybrid Mamba+attention models (Qwen3.5/3.6) initially errored ('TurboQuant KV cache is not supported for hybrid... models') with a merged fix following per r/LocalLLaMA [uncertain: fix PR number not confirmed]. The docs matrix now carries a TURBOQUANT row at 'Any' compute capability. The vLLM study 'A First Comprehensive Study of TurboQuant' (2026-05-11, vLLM 0.20.2 commit 6ec9bbec3, Qwen3-30B-A3B on 2xH100 and Llama-3.3-70B on 4xH100) established the key architectural fact - TurboQuant compresses KV storage only and dequantizes to BF16 before attention (vs FP8's quantized compute) - and the quality ladder: k8v4 preserves accuracy (~52 percent AUC, within one std of BF16/FP8) but offers no real advantage over FP8; 4bit_nc ~96 percent accuracy recovery; k3v4_nc/3bit_nc degrade up to 8-30 points; capacity extends 2.3-3.7x at 40-52 percent throughput reduction, 10-68 percent latency overhead, and burst P99 TTFT < 3.5s vs BF16 ~17s. Ecosystem momentum: llama.cpp port in flight (discussion #20969 with a working dependency-free CPU implementation, tracking issue #20977, PR #21089 adding tbq3_0 ~3.0625 and tbq4_0 ~4.0625 bits/element; ~4.57x KV compression enabling 72k-100k contexts on desktop GPUs per r/LocalLLaMA); community vLLM stack varjoranta/turboquant-vllm (Varjosoft Oy, 80 stars, MIT) whose GQA/MHA KV compression was merged upstream via #38479 and which now targets weight compression (TQ3 scalar HIGGS: WHT + Lloyd-Max + per-group norm) and an MLA monkey-patch path, explicitly listing sm_75 (T4/RTX 2080) through sm_121 as targets, validated on vLLM 0.19-0.20 and 0.25.x (v0.13.12), with unusually candid regressions (TQ3 decode ~7-17 percent of BF16 - 'a memory win, not a speed win'; fused Triton kernel 10.5x over separate dequant+cuBLAS; 71 percent KV access-time reduction at 32k context); AMD ROCm blog productionizing TurboQuant on AMD GPUs; SGLang parallel effort #21618; follow-on compression PRs in vLLM (SpectralQuant #43475, KVarN #46613/#46812, HIGGS tracking #40069); vLLM issue #40094 (2026-04-17, OPEN, no response) shows the selection gaps that remain: turboquant_4bit_nc rejected by both TRITON_ATTN and FLASH_ATTN with 'kv_cache_dtype not supported' on an L4 dev build (the dtypes need the dedicated backend); Kaitchup reports instability and memory leaks in early adopter setups. (4) Native INT8/INT4 track: vLLM's official INT8 W8A8 docs state 'INT8 computation is supported on NVIDIA GPUs with compute capability > 7.5' and list Turing/Ampere/Ada/Hopper (Blackwell >= 10.0 excluded - 'use FP8 instead'), with the canonical recipe SmoothQuant (smoothing_strength 0.8) + GPTQModifier W8A8 through llm-compressor; the Red Hat Developer write-up 'Understanding W8A8 INT8 LLM quantization' (Sana Fayyaz, 2026-09-07, part 1) walks Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct from 14.96 GB to 8.0 GB (46 percent) via SmoothQuant alpha 0.8 on WikiText-2 (512 samples) + GPTQ, served in vLLM on an L40S with accuracy preserved across MMLU/ARC/HellaSwag/IFeval and a 33 percent generation-speedup headline (load-test detail deferred to part 2). Marlin-for-Turing (PR #29901, merged 2025-12-16) added INT8 m8n8k16 MMA atoms on sm75 and W4A8-INT8 activation support (author's 2080 Ti: w4a8-int8 ~0.0106 ms vs w4a16 ~0.0115 ms at m=1, n2048/k4096); this host measured INT8 IMMA at exactly 2x FP16 = 203 TOPS at locked 1455 MHz (MEMORY.md 2026-08-27). QServe/QoQ (arXiv:2405.04532, MLSys 2025, mit-han-lab/omniserve) remains the strongest published native sub-16-bit recipe (W4A8KV4: 4-bit weights, INT8 activations, 4-bit KV with INT8 attention compute) but targets A100/L40S only - no Turing support or testing. (5) W8A8-FP8 activations on Turing: nobody does it. vLLM's FP8 docs are explicit that FP8 checkpoints on cc >= 7.5 degrade to weight-only W8A16 via FP8 Marlin - activations stay FP16; no upstream or known-community path rounds activations onto the E4M3 grid and computes in FP16. Faithful W8A8 emulation (stage 6) is fork-unique; its closest validation in the ecosystem is TurboQuant's storage-only-compression pattern (quantize the store, compute wide), which proves the pattern's deployment value but not the numerics of grid-rounded activations. INT8 KV without per-token-head plumbing does not exist upstream: issue #33480 (2026-01-31, OPEN, feature request, no responses) asks for INT8 KV precisely because 'KV cache quantization currently only supports FP8'; the only INT8 KV path today is TRITON_ATTN's int8/int4/fp8_per_token_head dtypes (the docs matrix lists TRITON_ATTN as the only backend with them), which community evidence places on Ampere ('int8 is the only KV-quant path for Gemma-4 on Ampere', issues #49716/#50749 - both open correctness bugs on hybrid-attention models).
lacuna.sm75_viability: What runs on Turing-class hardware today, with the real blockers. (1) Measured capability floors on this host (TU102/Quadro RTX 6000, locked 1455 MHz, MEMORY.md 2026-08-27): FP16 tensor ceiling ~101.7 TFLOP/s with FP32 accumulate; INT8 IMMA exactly 2x FP16 at 203 TOPS - the only native sub-16-bit tensor-core math on this silicon; DRAM 535 GB/s; no BF16, no cp.async below sm80, every ALU kind contends with the HMMA stream (16 ALU ops per 4 HMMAs drop it to ~24 percent); INT4 tensor MMA unsanctioned (ptxas rejects .s4 mma m8n8k16 on sm75 - INT4 is dp4a/register-dequant territory only); dp4a is available on the CUDA cores (sm61+ ISA fact) as the non-tensor int8 dot path. (2) The attention-backend candidate matrix for quantized KV on sm75, assembled from the docs matrix plus the live issues: TRITON_ATTN is the only auto-selected backend on sm75 post-v0.24.0; its documented KV dtypes are auto/fp16/bf16/fp8 flavors plus int4/int8/fp8_per_token_head at 'Any' compute capability - but the fp8 entries conflict with runtime reality on sm75, where v0.24.0 raises 'FP8 KV cache is not supported by the Triton attention backend... native FP8 (fp8e4nv) requires SM89+' (#47549), because Triton's fp8e4nv hard-requires SM89+ (the same floor SageAttention/ComfyUI users hit: 'SM89 kernel is not available'); int8 KV involves no fp8 dtype, so the Triton int8-load + scale + fp16-math path is sm75-legal in principle and is the only remaining upstream KV-quant door on Turing [uncertain: no verified sm75 run of int8_per_token_head exists; its known-good evidence is Ampere (Gemma-4, #49716/#50749), and those open hybrid-attention corruption bugs gate it]; FLASHINFER is documented 8.x-9.x and deselected on sm75 since v0.24.0 (#47549), and even forced it currently fails sm75 prefill with the 64 KB shared-memory overflow (FlashInfer #3620, fix PR #3621 open); FLASH_ATTN FA2 requires >= 8.0 - which also matters inside TurboQuant, whose prefill stage calls flash_attn_varlen_func: on sm75 that stage needs a Triton substitution before the backend works at all [uncertain: no sm75 TurboQuant run has been demonstrated upstream]; the TURBOQUANT backend row itself is marked 'Any' compute capability, and its k8v4 preset stores K in FP8 with a Triton dtype auto-select of float8e4nv (Hopper+) vs float8e4b15 (Ampere) - sm75 is unlisted, and would have to ride the float8e4b15 software-conversion route or substitute int8 [uncertain: float8e4b15 acceptance on sm75 in current Triton not verified here]. (3) Triton codegen path: on sm75 Triton lowers tensor math to mma.884/FMA with known floors (per host records: pinned <= 3.2 in past items, N-alignment surfaces) - TurboQuant's kernels are int-storage + WHT rotations + fp16 math, unusually sm75-compatible by construction, but bf16 intermediate usage degrades to emulation on Turing. (4) What the fork's stages 6-7 need none of: stage 7 recast is E4M3-KV stored 1-byte and dequantized to fp16 in the attention kernel - the E4M3-in-FP16 lossless-subset machinery from plan/0005 (LUT/rebias) plus the retained Turing engine (stage 11, load-bearing: without it nothing serves); stage 6 grid-rounding of activations is pure fp16 arithmetic (injective grid map, exact in float64); the INT8 native track rides the already-landed INT8 Marlin atoms (#29901) and the documented cc > 7.5 INT8 W8A8 floor. The one upstream number set for the FP8-KV value proposition on sm75 silicon is #47549's own: fp8 KV on Quadro RTX 8000 bought 287,744 vs ~143,000 tokens of capacity and 5-11 vs 0.8-1.1 tok/s decode at 22k context - a 2x-capacity, ~10x-throughput swing on cards identical in class to this host's.
lacuna.upstream_base: Dated ledger for the sm75 FP8-KV/activation surface. 2024-05: QServe/QoQ W4A8KV4 (arXiv:2405.04532, MLSys 2025; mit-han-lab/omniserve) - INT8 compute + 4-bit KV, A100/L40S only, never sm75. 2025-04-28: TurboQuant arXiv:2504.19874 v1 (Zandieh, Daliri, Hadian, Mirrokni). 2025-12-16: vLLM PR #29901 Marlin-for-Turing - INT8 m8n8k16 atoms, W4A8-INT8 activations, and FP8 weight-only W8A16 on sm75 (first release v0.14.0, tag 2026-01-16); INT8 W8A8 docs floor 'compute capability > 7.5' incl. Turing. 2026-01-31: issue #33480 opens the still-unanswered INT8-KV feature request. 2026-03-24: Google Research TurboQuant blog (ICLR 2026 acceptance; 3-bit near-lossless claim). 2026-03-29/04-15: vLLM PR #38479 opened/merged - dedicated TurboQuantAttentionBackend, 4 presets, Triton store/decode + flash_attn_varlen_func prefill [uncertain: first tagged vLLM release carrying #38479 not independently confirmed - the 2026-05-11 study pinned v0.20.2 at commit 6ec9bbec3, and v0.21.0 tagged 2026-05-14]. 2026-04-17: issue #40094 - turboquant dtypes rejected by TRITON_ATTN/FLASH_ATTN (L4). 2026-04-22: vLLM FP8-KV state blog (H100/B200 only; FA3 accumulation fix; skip-layers #33695). 2026-05-11: vLLM TurboQuant comprehensive study (storage-only compression; quality/perf ladder). 2026-06-12: FlashInfer #3620 - sm75 prefill shared-memory overflow (P1; PR #3621 open). 2026-06-29 (approx): vLLM v0.24.0 released (571 commits; per-KV-cache-group backend selection #48012) - FlashInfer no longer offered on sm75; fp8 KV on sm75 now raises the fp8e4nv/SM89+ ValueError. 2026-07-03: issue #47549 filed (OPEN, unassigned; suspected cause PR #46492 [uncertain: reporter's attribution]). 2026-09-07: Red Hat W8A8 INT8 write-up (SmoothQuant+GPTQ, llm-compressor, vLLM serving). Last-good bases for the fork: v0.23.0 + flashinfer-python 0.6.12 (the last upstream combination where FP8 KV worked on sm75, via software conversion - the natural baseline for stage-7 recast comparisons); PR #38479 (2026-04-15) for the TurboQuant backend (rebasable onto fork pin 79378fe6e8 with a prefill substitution); #29901-era Marlin INT8 (still current upstream per the w4a16 item ledger).

effort_value.effort_estimate: Two short campaigns plus two optional extensions, in dependency order. (1) Stage 7 FP8-KV recast - days: an E4M3-KV storage layout (1 byte/element, per-tensor or per-head scale) in the fork's retained Turing engine's attention path, dequant-in-flight via the plan/0005 LUT/rebias machinery; serving-config record of required dtype; oracle is exact by construction (E4M3 is a subset of FP16). (2) INT8-KV variant + upstream probe - one to two sessions: probe TRITON_ATTN int8_per_token_head acceptance on the Quadro RTX 6000, then either adopt it or mirror it in the fork's attention kernel with per-head scales; quality-measured against fp16-KV per the stage-7 contract. (3) Stage 6 W8A8-emulated - one to two weeks: runtime per-token dynamic quantization hook at the layer boundary (amax -> E4M3 grid rounding, values kept in fp16), riding existing GEMM strategy rows; float64-oracle with the grid-rounding reference (exact); ladder-tuned only if a speed question exists (expected none - fp16 compute either way; the deliverable is numerics faithfulness and future-FP8-silicon readiness). (4) Native INT8 track - days to a week: stand up the llm-compressor SmoothQuant+GPTQ W8A8 recipe (Red Hat part-1 as template, 512-sample calibration) on an 8B model, serve through the INT8-capable Marlin paths already at the pin, measure against the 203-TOPS wall. (5) TurboQuant port (optional successor, weeks): rebase PR #38479's TurboQuantAttentionBackend onto the fork, replace flash_attn_varlen_func prefill with a Triton prefill (sm80+ floor of FA2), substitute k8v4's FP8-K Triton dtype (int8 or float8e4b15) for sm75, and gate exposure to k8v4/4bit_nc only per the 2026-05-11 study's quality ladder.
effort_value.unlocks: Stage 7 doubles KV capacity on 24 GB cards for every model the fork serves - the #47549 measurement prices it: 287,744 vs ~143,000 tokens and 5-11 vs 0.8-1.1 tok/s decode on identical silicon - and directly unblocks the operator's long-context serving targets (plan/0005's Qwen3-class 27B both-card run 'with generous KV'; 100k-class contexts become planable); it also re-opens the FP8-KV door that upstream closed for every sm75 user (T4 through RTX 8000, AWS g4dn included), which is externally defensible fork value. Stage 6 completes the format ladder: W8A8-FP8 checkpoints become faithfully studiable on Turing (activation-grid effects, per-token scale policy, outlier handling) informing the W8A8-INT8-native vs W8A8-FP8-emulated choice for the operator's checkpoints, and pre-validates numerics for any future sm89+ hardware. The INT8 track activates Turing's only native sub-16-bit compute (measured 203 TOPS, 2x the fp16 ceiling) with an upstream-documented Turing floor and a fresh Red Hat recipe - the on-ramp to a QServe-class W4A8KV4 recipe on this silicon. The TurboQuant extension is the strongest long-context lever per the outline: 2.6-3.8x KV capacity at 4-bit quality floors the ecosystem has now measured publicly, on a Triton-first design unusually suited to sm75.
effort_value.dependency_order: Must land first: plan/0005 stages 1-3 (checkpoint adapters, E4M3 recast loader, LUT/rebias dequant machinery - stage 7 is a direct consumer) and the retained Turing engine health (stage 11 - load-bearing: every KV-dtype path needs a serving engine; upstream offers none on sm75 post-v0.24.0). The float64-oracle + ladder + winner-gate harness (plan/0003) is landed. Stage 7 recast and the INT8 probe are independent of stage 6 and of each other - parallelizable immediately. Stage 6 depends on stage-1 adapters (FP8 checkpoint parse incl. activation-scale layouts) and the plan/0004 scale machinery for per-token scales; its runtime quantization hook is the only genuinely new component. The INT8 track depends only on llm-compressor (pip) and the INT8 Marlin paths already at the fork pin. The TurboQuant extension depends on stage 7 (KV-layout lessons), engine health, and a rebase of PR #38479 (Apr 2026) onto the pin - schedule last. External prerequisites: none for stages 6-7 and INT8 (all primitives sm75-sanctioned: LUT/rebias, fp16 MMA, INT8 IMMA, dp4a); flashinfer-python 0.6.12 wheels only if the v0.23.0 FlashInfer software-conversion baseline is reproduced for comparison.
effort_value.risk_notes: Numerics: (1) FP8-KV quality is context-dependent - the vLLM 2026-04-22 study shows near-baseline only with fixes and calibration: avoid sub-7k-token contexts, head_dim-256 prefill, and uncalibrated per-tensor scales below 95 percent recovery; the FA3 FP32-accumulation bug (91 -> 13 -> 89 percent NIAH) was a hardware-path bug absent from fp16-computed emulation, but its lesson - long-context accumulation depth - transfers to any fp16 flash-attention decode at 64k+, so the fork's KV-recast decode needs an accumulation-order review at K=64k+ before quality claims. (2) Stage 6 faithfulness boundary: rounding activations onto the E4M3 grid loses outliers (E4M3 max 448) - per-token dynamic scales are mandatory, and static-scale checkpoints may need SmoothQuant-style smoothing; fp16 compute of grid-rounded activations reproduces the quantized values exactly but NOT native-sm89 FP8 MMA accumulation order - the emulation is faithful to values, not to native arithmetic, and must be labeled as such or numerics claims silently diverge. (3) TurboQuant quality is preset-dependent (2026-05-11 study: k8v4 fine but redundant vs FP8; k3v4_nc/3bit_nc lose 8-30 points on reasoning benchmarks) - expose 4bit_nc/k8v4 only; the upstream port omits QJL residual correction that the paper uses for K, and norm-correction centroid renorm is an extra correctness surface; hybrid/sliding-window models are unsupported upstream with open corruption bugs on the int8_per_token_head path (#49716/#50749). Silent-fallback risks: the #47549 class - backend selection silently dropping a working path on sm75; the docs-matrix-vs-runtime conflict (TRITON_ATTN fp8 listed 'Any' but rejected on sm75) proves capability claims need runtime probes, not doc reads; TurboQuant prefill's flash_attn_varlen_func dependency fails quietly on sm75 if the substitution is missed. Upstream drift: TurboQuant surface churns fast (#40069 tracker, #40792/#41422/#41803 follow-ups, Qwen3.5+ fix) - pin-and-rebase cadence; #47549 and FlashInfer #3620/#3621 are open and could move the sm75 baseline in either direction; INT8 is dead-ended on Blackwell upstream (>= 10.0 excluded), so the native track is Turing-local value [uncertain: amax reductions in the Triton store kernels may use atomics - tie-breaking run-to-run variance unverified].
effort_value.determinism_class: Stage 7 recast and stage 6 grid-rounding are bitwise-deterministic by construction: E4M3 quantization is an injective grid map (float64 reference exact), E4M3 -> FP16 dequant is lossless (subset; LUT/rebias injective), so the float64-oracle gate can demand bit-exactness for the quantize/dequantize pair and 2x passes are meaningful. Attention over recast KV: fp16 flash-style accumulation order is fixed per kernel config (deterministic run-to-run), but it differs from any native-FP8 accumulation order - cross-checks against upstream FP8-KV runs are statistical, not bitwise, and belong in the median-of-N discipline rather than exact-diff gates. Per-token dynamic scales: deterministic for fixed inputs provided the amax reduction is staged/fixed-order; if implemented with atomics the reduction order varies run-to-run on ties - the winner-gate transcript must record which class the hook ships. INT8 IMMA GEMM: int32 exact accumulation, fixed tile traversal - bitwise per config; SmoothQuant calibration is an offline deterministic pass (fixed data, fixed seeds). TurboQuant: WHT rotations and Lloyd-Max codebook lookups are deterministic and training-free (no calibration randomness); the known nondeterminism-adjacent defect class is CUDA-graph interaction (the upstream token-loop bug #40831 fixed in #40914 - replay-ordering), so any ported store/decode kernels need the fork's cuda-graph validation replay re-run. KV-cache writes are appends per token (no atomics) - not a variance source. Restart-to-restart: stable given same inputs and graphs; fresh-process state (scales, cache) is caller-zeroed per the standing workspace contract.

decision.priority_signal: For doing this next: the regression hole is live and unaddressed upstream - #47549 has sat open since 2026-07-03 with no maintainer response while every sm75 user's FP8 KV collapsed to a ~10x decode penalty, and restoring software-converted FP8 KV (or better, recast KV) on the retained engine is exactly the fork's stated value proposition with a measured 287k-vs-143k-token, 5-11-vs-0.8-1.1-tok/s payoff on same-class silicon; stage 7 is days of work on landed machinery (E4M3 LUT/rebias from plan/0005 stages 1-3); the INT8 native track has an upstream-documented Turing floor, a fresh Red Hat recipe (2026-09-07), and rides the 203-TOPS measured advantage; TurboQuant gives the 24 GB long-context endgame (2.6-3.8x capacity at measured quality floors) with an sm75-friendly Triton-first upstream implementation (#38479, docs 'Any' compute capability) and a community port already targeting sm_75. Against: stage 6 buys zero speed on this silicon (fp16 compute either way) - its value is format-interop completeness and future-silicon prep, so it ranks below stage 7; the TurboQuant port is weeks with a churning upstream surface and its own prefill substitution problem; FP8 KV itself may be superseded by TurboQuant-class compression (3.8-4.9x > 2x) if 4-bit quality holds, which argues for going straight to 4bit_nc rather than perfecting fp8. Window-closing: medium - #47549 being open cuts both ways (upstream may restore FlashInfer sm75 selection any week, closing the differentiation window for the restore path specifically, though not for recast/oracle-quality/TurboQuant); TurboQuant is mainstreaming fast (llama.cpp PR, AMD production blog, SGLang effort), so the port window is now. Net: stage 7 + INT8 probe next (small, high-value, unblocked); stage 6 after the stage 1-3 machinery lands; TurboQuant as stage 7's successor once engine health is banked.
decision.recommended_probe: Gate-0, oracle-first, no timing until numerics pass - three cheap probes. (1) Stage-7 recast probe (one session): on the retained Turing engine with an 8B fp16 model, insert an E4M3 quantize->dequantize round-trip on K and V at store time (fp16 storage of grid-rounded values, per-tensor scale = amax/448); assert bit-exactness against a float64 oracle applying the same grid map, then measure the quality delta vs unquantized fp16 KV on a fixed eval (GSM8K 250-sample + one long-context retrieval set, mirroring the vLLM study methodology) - this settles 'FP8-KV recast at 2x memory is quality-neutral on real attention kernels' before any 1-byte-storage kernel work. (2) sm75 KV-dtype acceptance matrix (one session, upstream builds, no fork code): on the Quadro RTX 6000 run pinned v0.23.0 with --kv-cache-dtype fp8 (FlashInfer software-conversion baseline - the last working upstream sm75 FP8 KV) and current vLLM/fork pin with fp8 (expected SM89+ ValueError), int8_per_token_head, and turboquant_4bit_nc (expected backend rejection per #40094) on a small GQA model; record which dtype/backend pairs launch, token capacity, and tok/s at 16-32k context - this maps the real sm75 acceptance surface that #47549/#40094 only partially show and prices the regression hole in this host's own numbers. (3) Stage-6 grid probe (half session, pure PyTorch, no kernels): per-token dynamic E4M3 rounding of activations at layer boundaries on one fp16 model; quality-diff vs baseline on the same eval - settles whether faithful W8A8 emulation needs SmoothQuant-style static smoothing or per-token dynamic scales suffice, before the runtime hook is designed. All three produce oracle transcripts plus eval deltas; timing only after numerics gates pass, per the standing rules.
